Sasha: heads up — nv-gpu-pool is showing sustained queue growth, admission controller has bumped throttles. thinking about switching from a static TPM to an SLO‑driven TPM that reacts to 95th pct queue latency.
Liam: can you paste the current numbers? how far over SLO are we?
Sasha: 95p queue latency ~1.4s (SLO = 1.0s). pool usable GPUs = 42 (some nodes draining), avg tokens/sec per GPU ~= 38 for chat workload. current global TPM cap = 95,000.
Olivia: rough math: TPM should track available capacity. if each GPU sustains ~38 tok/s -> per GPU TPM ~38*60 = 2280 tok/min. 42 GPUs -> 95,760 TPM, so current cap is about right on capacity but doesn't account for queuing + headroom.
Liam: right, we need headroom for burst and sys overhead (kv cache, preemption). proposal: make TPM = floor((sum_effective_gpu_tokps) * 60 * headroom_factor) and adjust headroom_factor based on SLO.
Sasha: i prototyped an EWMA controller that nudges headroom_factor between 0.75 and 1.25 depending on 95p latency. pseudo:```
// every 30s
error = max(0, observed_95p_latency - target_latency)
delta = k * error
headroom = clamp(headroom - delta, 0.75, 1.25)
TPM = floor(effective_tokps_sum * 60 * headroom)
```
Olivia: love the simplicity. what is k? tuning param?
Sasha: yep, small (0.02) so changes are gradual. also add a cooldown to prevent oscillation when nodes come up/down.
Liam: need safety constraints: a lower hard floor (so we don't kill background batch jobs) and a short emergency spike token bucket for handoffs. maybe: reserve = max(5000, 0.05 * TPM) and emergency_burst = min(20000, 0.2 * TPM).
Sasha: agreed. also we should weight regional TPMs so global clients don't deplete one region: apply regional_weight = region_capacity / total_capacity then regional_TPM = global_TPM * regional_weight.
Olivia: note net effects: if a region drains GPUs due to preemption, its regional_weight falls and traffic gets routed (if policy allows) to sibling regions. we need to ensure routing fallback respects data residency.
infra-bot: runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/tpm-adaptive (created by Sasha) :page_facing_up:
Liam: operational checklist before flipping on autopilot: 1) add observability: token burn rate, queue length, 95/99 lat; 2) add circuit-breaker to disable adaptive logic if control loop misbehaves; 3) simulation with synthetic load; 4) small canary (10% traffic).
Sasha: i'll open a PR with controller code + dashboards. also want to log every TPM change event with reason and recent latency snapshot.
Olivia: one more thought on accounting: our current token model counts input+output tokens equally. for chat we should weight output tokens higher (x1.2) to reflect GPU generation cost. that shifts TPM math slightly.
Liam: good catch. also confirm how reserved capacity (dedicated customers) interacts — their tokens should be carved out before adaptive pool math.
Sasha: yes reserved gets priority. adaptive controller operates on the remaining shared tokens.
Olivia: sounds good. if we can validate stability in sim, i'm +1 to roll out to nv on canary next week. :rocket: 
Sasha: will schedule sim and open PR today. tagging @oncall for FYI.
